{"subject": "organizational changes", "body": "changes in enron ' s business require us to reevaluate how we approach the
engineering and construction function within enron . specifically , enron
energy services ' ( ees ) business has grown dramatically and that requires
considerable additional engineering and construction resources both to
develop solutions for customers and to deliver those solutions to customers .
additionally , in light of enron ' s continued emphasis on increasing our return
on invested capital , we have been engaged in fewer large scale construction
projects around the world . historically , these projects have been a primary
focus of eecc ' s activities . consequently we are making the following
organizational changes concerning eecc :
eecc ' s pipeline construction group , led by jerry martin , will become part of
enron transportation services .
nepco will continue to operate as a stand alone entity focused on power plant
construction services to enron entities and third parties .
the remainder of eecc will become part of ees . larry izzo will report to the
ees office of the chairman .
these changes will better align our intellectual capital with the growth
opportunities within enron and provide new and exciting opportunities for our
employees . please join us in supporting and implementing these changes ."}

{"subject": "california update 6 / 08 / 01", "body": "cpuc delays qf payment vote\nsources believe that the delay in the puc vote on paying the qfs 15 % of their undercollected debt is likely a result from both a concern about bankruptcy issues raised by issuing what could be seen as a \" preference payment \" to the qfs ( the puc does follow these issues out of necessity , given the current environment ) and a lack of clarity regarding how to implement the 15 % payment . the delay was unsurprising and characteristic of how the puc operates . it is also noted that there are many claims on socal ' s and pg & e ' s cash flows currently . additionally , agreeing to pay 15 % of debts to the qfs raises legal issues , in that the utilities would be paying debts to some creditors , but not others . this could increase the likelihood of an involuntary bankruptcy filing against socal by the non - qf creditors ."}

{"subject": "The Saturday Fork: Pierogi pop-up, a pear tart recipe, and where to get good bread in Millbrook", "body": "Hi neighbours,

Welcome to this week's Saturday Fork, your digest of what's cooking around Millbrook.

THE BIG NEWS
Babka & Barrel, the little bakery on Ostrander Lane, is finally open on Sundays. Go early. The cardamom knots sell out by 9:30.

POP-UP ALERT
Chef Danuta Wroblewski is running a pierogi pop-up at the Tin Roof Taproom this Thursday and Friday, 5-9pm. Potato and cheese, sauerkraut and mushroom, and a sweet farmer's cheese with blueberry sauce. $12 for a plate of eight.

RECIPE OF THE WEEK: Brown butter pear tart
Pears are at their best at the Wednesday market. Full recipe on the blog, but the short version: brown the butter until it smells like toasted hazelnuts, and don't skip the pinch of salt in the crust.

READER QUESTION
"Where can I find good rye bread?" Several of you wrote in. Our top three picks are in this week's post.

See you at the market,
Marguerite
The Saturday Fork

Unsubscribe any time at the bottom of this email."}

{"subject": "Harbor Striders Update: Turkey Trot signups, new Tuesday route", "body": "Hey Striders!

Quick club update before the holiday rush.

1. TURKEY TROT
Registration for our annual 5K is open. Thanksgiving morning, 8:30am start at Pier 4. Costumes encouraged. Last year's gravy-boat trophy is still at large, so someone please bring it back.

2. TUESDAY RUNS
Due to construction on Alder Street, the Tuesday evening run now starts from the library parking lot and follows the river path. Same time, 6:15pm. Bring a headlamp, it's getting dark early.

3. PACE GROUPS
We now have a 10:30+ min/mile group led by Tomás. Everyone welcome, nobody gets left behind.

4. VOLUNTEERS NEEDED
We need six people for water station duty on Nov 22. Reply to this email if you can help.

See you on the road,
Priya, Harbor Striders Club Secretary"}

{"subject": "November at the Halvorsen Museum of Regional History", "body": "Dear Friends of the Halvorsen,

November brings shorter days and, we hope, longer visits.

NEW EXHIBIT
"Salt, Sail & Cannery: Life on the Northern Coast" opens Nov 8 in the East Gallery. Over 200 objects, including a restored fishing dory and letters from cannery workers.

THIS MONTH'S EVENTS
Nov 9, 2pm: Curator talk with Dr. Ines Abara
Nov 15, 10am: Family Saturday: build your own paper boat
Nov 21, 7pm: Evening lecture, "Lighthouses of the Coast" (members free, $8 general)
Nov 29: Late-night opening until 9pm

MEMBERS' CORNER
Members get early access to the winter workshop series starting Dec 1. Register by Nov 20.

HOURS
Tue-Sun, 10am-5pm. Closed Mondays and Nov 27.

Warmly,
The Halvorsen Museum Visitor Team"}

{"subject": "Cedar Hollow Neighbours Bulletin – November", "body": "CEDAR HOLLOW NEIGHBOURHOOD ASSOCIATION
November Bulletin

LEAF COLLECTION
City crews will collect bagged leaves on Nov 12 and Nov 26. Paper bags only, please, set out by 7am.

STREETLIGHT OUTAGE
The light at the corner of Birch and 4th has been out for three weeks. A repair request has been filed (ref #55812). If you notice others, tell us.

ANNUAL MEETING
Thursday Nov 19, 7pm at the Community Hall. Agenda: budget, the proposed speed bumps on Willow Court, and election of two board members. Cookies provided by the Pruitt family, as always.

LOST & FOUND
A grey tabby named Biscuit has been missing since Oct 30. Please check sheds and garages.

Best,
George Ndlovu, Secretary"}

{"subject": "Thread & Needle Weekly: knitting patterns, a yarn sale, and a confession", "body": "Hello fellow makers!

I have a confession: I've started four sweaters and finished none. If that sounds familiar, this week's issue is for you.

PATTERN OF THE WEEK
The Lantern Cowl, a beginner-friendly one-skein project. Done in an evening, perfect for gifts. Free for subscribers through Sunday.

SALE
Woolly Pines Yarn Co. (my favourite little shop, no affiliation beyond love) is taking 20% off all worsted weight through Nov 10.

TIP
When your edges curl, blocking is your friend. A spray bottle and a few pins will fix most sins.

COMMUNITY
Many of you asked about a knit-along. Starting Nov 15 we'll be making the Harvest Shawl together. Join the thread on the forum.

Happy stitching,
Beatrix"}

{"subject": "Night Sky Notes: Leonids, a quiet Moon, and Saturn's rings", "body": "Greetings stargazers,

The Leonid meteor shower peaks on the night of Nov 17-18. With a thin crescent Moon this year, skies should be nicely dark. Expect around 10-15 meteors per hour from a dark site after midnight.

THIS MONTH'S TARGETS
- Saturn: visible in the south after sunset. Its rings appear very thin this year, a rare treat.
- Pleiades: rising in the east by 8pm. Binoculars reveal dozens of stars.

CLUB NEWS
Our next observing night is Nov 14 at Marsh Ridge, weather permitting. Dress warmly, bring a red flashlight, and a thermos.

GEAR CORNER
Thinking about a first telescope? A 6-inch Dobsonian is hard to beat for the price.

Clear skies,
Oliver Prasad, Eastfield Astronomy Society"}

{"subject": "Your Money, Plainly: November issue", "body": "Hi there,

This month in Your Money, Plainly:

1. WHAT IS AN I-BOND-STYLE SAVINGS PRODUCT, ANYWAY?
A straightforward explainer on inflation-linked savings, who they suit, and who they don't.

2. YEAR-END CHECKLIST
Before Dec 31: review your retirement contributions, check your flexible spending balance, and gather charitable receipts.

3. READER MAILBAG
"Should I pay off my car loan early?" Short answer: it depends on the rate. We walk through the math.

4. ONE SMALL HABIT
Schedule a 15-minute monthly money check-in. Same day, same coffee.

This newsletter is educational and not personalised financial advice.

Cheers,
Deborah Lindqvist"}

{"subject": "Paws & Whiskers Rescue: Adoptable pets + winter drive", "body": "Hello friends of Paws & Whiskers,

MEET THIS MONTH'S STARS
Cooper, 3-year-old beagle mix, loves car rides and belly rubs.
Miso, 1-year-old black cat, shy at first but a champion cuddler.
Peanut and Pickle, bonded pair of guinea pigs looking for a home together.

With gratitude,
The Paws & Whiskers team"}

{"subject": "Library Lines: new arrivals and book club pick for Nov", "body": "Dear patrons,

Fiction: "The Glassmaker's Daughter" by R. Okonkwo-Hale; "Tidewater" by Linnea Frost.
Non-fiction: "A Short History of Salt" by Jorge Medina.

Calder Street Branch Library"}

{"subject": "The Tuesday Plate: Quince season, a dumpling crawl, and one very good bakery closing", "body": "Hello, hungry neighbours,

This week's digest from Plate & Pavement.

THE BIG NEWS
Brennig's Bakehouse on Alder Row is closing its doors on 22 November after 14 years. Owner Dilys Brennig says she's retiring to Anglesey to "sleep past 3 a.m. for the first time since 2012." Go and get a loaf of the caraway rye while you can. Her final week will feature a different laminated pastry every day.

WHAT WE ATE
- Little Tamsin's Dumpling House (Corrin Street): the pork and chive pan-fried dumplings are crisp on the bottom and properly juicy. Eight for £7.50. The chilli oil is made in-house and is not shy. 4.5/5
- Fennimore's Pantry: a quince and almond tart that tasted like autumn in a good way. They sell the quince paste separately now.
- The new lunch counter at Ostler & Daughters: skip the soup, order the lentil salad.

DUMPLING CRAWL
Saturday 14 November, 12:00. We'll hit four spots in the Corrin Street area, about 2 hours, roughly £25 all in. Reply to this email to save a place. 12 spots only.

RECIPE OF THE WEEK
Baked quince with honey and bay. Peel, halve and core 4 quinces. Arrange in a dish with 3 tbsp honey, 2 bay leaves, a splash of white wine and 300 ml water. Cover with foil and bake at 160°C for 2 hours until rosy. Serve with thick yoghurt.

See you next Tuesday,
Marguerite
Plate & Pavement

{"subject": "Harrow Lane Striders – November update (and yes, the Turkey Trot is back)", "body": "Hi Striders,

Quick update before the weekend.

REGULAR RUNS
Tuesday 18:30 – intervals at the track (Millbrook Rec). Bring a headtorch for the warm-up lap.
Thursday 18:30 – social 5K from the Anchor & Hope. Pace groups: 6:00, 7:00, "chatty."
Sunday 08:30 – long run. This week: 16 km out to Whitcombe Reservoir and back.

{"subject": "The Quince Issue: jelly, regrets, and a very sticky stove", "body": "Hello again, fellow snackers,

I said I would never make quince jelly a second time. Last autumn it took six hours, ruined a tea towel, and my neighbour Odile still brings it up. And yet here I am, with 4 kg of lumpy yellow fruit from the Marchetti allotment and a stove that now has a permanent amber glaze.

This issue:

1) THE RECIPE: Lazy Quince Paste (membrillo, more or less)
Peel, core, and chop 1 kg quince. Simmer in just enough water until soft, about 35 minutes. Blend, weigh the purée, and add 75% of that weight in sugar. Cook on low, stirring constantly, for 40-50 minutes until it pulls away from the pot. Pour into a lined tin and leave overnight. Serve with salty cheese. Wear long sleeves because the purée spits like an angry cat.

2) WHERE I ATE THIS MONTH
- Tamsin's Hatch (behind the Corn Exchange): the leek and mustard toastie is the best thing I have eaten in 2026. Cash only, closes when the bread runs out, usually 1:30.

3) MARKET NEWS

4) READER MAIL

See you in two weeks. Eat something with butter in it.

Marguerite

{"subject": "The November sky: Leonids, a late Saturn, and how to see Mars before dawn", "body": "ORMEROD ASTRONOMICAL SOCIETY
Monthly Observing Notes - November 2026

Greetings, stargazers.

PLANETS
Saturn is still well placed in the southern evening sky, setting around midnight early in the month. Its rings are quite thin at the moment, tilted nearly edge-on from our viewpoint, so don't expect the classic postcard view. Jupiter rises in the evening and dominates the late-night sky. Mars appears in the pre-dawn east. Venus is lost in the Sun's glare.

METEORS
The Leonids peak overnight on 17-18 November. Expect around 10-15 meteors per hour under dark skies. The Moon is a waning crescent and will not interfere much. Best viewing is after midnight, when the radiant in Leo is high. Dress warmly and bring a reclining chair.

DEEP SKY TARGETS
- M31 (Andromeda Galaxy): high in the evening, visible to the naked eye from dark sites.
- The Double Cluster in Perseus: spectacular in binoculars.
- NGC 457, the 'Owl Cluster' in Cassiopeia: a good one for small telescopes.

SOCIETY NEWS
- Public observing night: Sat 14 Nov, 7 pm, Kettlewell Field. Cloud-cancelled notices go out by 5 pm on the day.
- Monthly meeting: Wed 25 Nov, 7:30 pm. Talk: 'Measuring the Hubble Constant with a Cardboard Tube', by Dr. Anya Voss.
- The 8-inch Dobsonian is available for loan to members. Please sign it out and return it clean.

Clear skies,
Frank Delaney, Newsletter Editor

{"subject": "Hive Notes: preparing colonies for the cold snap", "body": "Halvorsen Valley Beekeepers' Society, monthly letter

Dear members,

With the first frost behind us, now is the time to check your hives are winter-ready.

CHECKLIST
- Mouse guards on every entrance by the end of this week
- Heft the hives. A colony should feel heavy at the back. If it feels light, feed fondant, not syrup, now that it's cold
- Strap hives down if you're on the exposed ridge sites
- Ventilation matters more than insulation. Damp kills more bees than cold

VARROA
Oxalic acid trickle treatment is best done in December when the colony is broodless. We will run a hands-on demonstration at the apiary on Saturday December 6. Please bring your own gloves and goggles. Do not skip the goggles.

SOCIETY NEWS
Our honey show raised £412 for the equipment fund. Special mention to Wilhelmina Cho, whose heather honey took best in show for the third year running. Cries of "fix!" were good natured.

MENTORING
We have four new beekeepers without mentors. If you can spare an hour a month, please reply and let me know.

Keep warm, and let the bees alone,
Anders"}

{"subject": "Tidewatch: Saturday's fishing and tide report, Pellam Bay", "body": "TIDEWATCH WEEKLY | Pellam Bay Anglers' Digest

High tide Saturday: 6:42am / 7:08pm
Low tide: 12:55pm
Wind: SW 10-15 knots, easing in the afternoon
Water temp: 11.4C

WHAT'S BITING
Sea bass are still showing along the rocky breakwater at dusk. Soft plastics in natural colours, slow retrieve. Several of you reported mackerel off the pier, but they're thinning out. Whiting and small cod are picking up on lugworm from the beach at Stack Point.

A WARNING
The slipway at Quillen Cove has a large patch of weed and is slippery. Two anglers took a tumble last weekend, one of them our own Dennis. His pride is the only thing injured.

GEAR TIP
If your braid keeps tangling in the cold, try a thin coat of line conditioner before each trip. It makes a real difference.

CLUB
Winter match league begins December 7. Entry is £5 and includes tea and a bacon roll. Sign up with Maureen at the tackle shop.

Tight lines,
The Tidewatch crew"}

2. Brindle & Rye Bakery has restarted its sourdough rye after a two-month break. Loaves sell out by 10 a.m. Ask for the dark crust.

3. The Copper Ladle's new autumn menu. Skip the overpriced flatbread. Order the braised lamb neck with pickled quince and thank me later.

RECIPE CORNER: Lazy Quince Paste (membrillo)
Peel, core, and chop 1.5 kg of quince. Simmer with 1 kg sugar and the juice of a lemon for about 90 minutes, stirring more often as it thickens. Pour into a lined tin and let it set overnight. Serve with sharp cheese. It keeps for months, if you have the willpower.

See you at the market,
Tamsin

{"subject": "Tidewrack Weekly: what the tide tables won't tell you", "body": "Morning, fellow shore-walkers.

SPOTTED THIS WEEK
- A very confused seal near the harbour wall, Tuesday. It left of its own accord after about an hour. No need to call anyone unless it's still there after a full tide cycle.
- Lots of razor clam shells on the north beach after Sunday's surge.
- One (1) shopping trolley. Unclear how.

TIDES FOR THE COMING WEEK
High water roughly 06:12 and 18:35 on Saturday, with a big spring tide Monday. Stay off the causeway an hour either side.

BEACH CLEAN
Sunday 8 November, 10 a.m., meet at the lifeboat station. Gloves and bags supplied. Bring a flask.

A SMALL REQUEST
If you find a ringed bird, note the code and send it in. Last month a reader's photo helped us trace a curlew back to a marsh over 400 miles away.

Until next week,
Bryony

{"subject": "Starlight Society: Leonids on the 17th, a dark-sky night, and a mirror-grinding workshop", "body": "Hello stargazers,

A short, hopeful newsletter. The forecast for mid-November is looking clearer than usual, which for us is basically a miracle.

THIS MONTH IN THE SKY
- Leonid meteor shower peaks overnight on 17 to 18 November. Expect around 10 to 15 meteors an hour from a dark site. The Moon will be a thin waning crescent, so conditions are good.
- Jupiter is well placed in the evening sky. Even small telescopes will show the four Galilean moons.
- Look low in the east before dawn for the bright star Regulus, near the crescent Moon on the 14th.

OBSERVING NIGHTS
Friday 13 November, 7 p.m. onwards, at Croften Common car park. We'll have the society's 10-inch Dobsonian and a couple of smaller scopes. Bring warm layers, a red torch, and a hot drink. If it's cloudy we'll move to the pub, as tradition dictates.

WORKSHOP
Saturday 28 November, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Grind your own 6-inch telescope mirror with guidance from Warrick Ibe. Materials £45. Spaces are limited to eight, and no experience is needed.

MEMBERS' PHOTOS
Huge congratulations to Odalys Brennock, whose picture of the Andromeda Galaxy was picked as image of the month. Send us your own shots by the 25th.

Clear skies,
The Starlight Society committee"}

{"subject": "Parcelwise 4.8 release notes", "body": "Parcelwise 4.8.0 is now available.

HIGHLIGHTS
* Batch label printing: select up to 200 shipments and print in one PDF.
* New webhook event `shipment.delayed`, fired when a carrier scan is overdue by more than 24 hours.
* The dashboard now supports dark mode. Toggle it under Settings > Appearance.

IMPROVEMENTS
* Address validation is about 30% faster for UK and Irish postcodes.
* CSV import now reports the row number for each error instead of a generic failure message.
* API responses include a `request_id` header to help with support tickets.

FIXES
* Fixed a bug where returns created after midnight UTC were dated the previous day.

The Parcelwise Team

{"subject": "Stargazer's Almanac: November sky notes", "body": "Clear skies, and welcome to this month's sky notes.

THE HIGHLIGHT
The Leonid meteor shower peaks overnight on 17-18 November. This year the Moon is a thin crescent that sets early, so conditions should be good after midnight. Expect 10 to 15 meteors an hour from a dark site. Dress warmly. Then dress warmer than that.

PLANETS
Saturn is well placed in the southern sky after dusk, with its rings tilted only slightly toward us. Jupiter rises around 8 pm and is bright enough to spot even from town.

DEEP SKY TARGET
Try the Double Cluster in Perseus. It's visible as a fuzzy patch to the naked eye and resolves into hundreds of stars in binoculars.

FROM THE OBSERVATORY
Our public viewing nights run Fridays at 7 pm, weather permitting. We check the forecast by 4 pm and post an update on the website.

BEGINNER TIP
Give your eyes 20 minutes to adapt to the dark and use a red light for reading charts. Even a brief look at a phone screen resets the clock.

Happy observing,
Nadia Kowalczyk
Edgemoor Amateur Astronomical Society"}

{"subject": "The Tuesday Tinker #88: soldering, sourdough and a weird little oscillator", "body": "Hey tinkerers,

This week's issue is a bit chaotic. Pour a coffee.

1. BUILD OF THE WEEK
Reader Samir sent in a pocket-sized oscillator built from a single 555 timer and some leftover resistors. It sounds like a very angry bee. Schematic and audio clip are on the site.

2. TOOL REVIEW
I tried a cheap temperature-controlled soldering iron (about £28). Heats up in under 30 seconds and the tip held up for three weeks of daily use. The cable is stiff, but that's the only real complaint. Verdict: worth it for beginners.

3. DETOUR
I've been baking sourdough with a 3D-printed proofing box. Not electronics, but there's a thermistor involved, so I'm counting it.

4. LINKS
- A clear guide to reading resistor colour codes without squinting
- A teardown of a thirty-year-old answering machine
- A thread on why your breadboard has probably gone bad

5. LISTENER QUESTION
'Is it safe to reuse old capacitors?' Short version: for low-voltage hobby projects, usually fine if they test good. For anything mains-related, don't.

See you next Tuesday,
Finn
The Tuesday Tinker"}

{"subject": "Quillbase 4.2.0 released: faster sync, new query filters, two breaking changes", "body": "Quillbase 4.2.0 is now available.

HIGHLIGHTS

* Sync engine rewrite: initial sync on large workspaces (50k+ notes) is roughly 3x faster in our benchmarks. Incremental sync now batches writes, which should reduce battery drain on laptops.
* Query filters: you can now use `before:`, `after:` and `linked-from:` in the search bar and in saved queries.
* Template variables: `{{cursor}}` places your caret after a template is inserted.
* Dark theme refinements: improved contrast for code blocks and block quotes.

BREAKING CHANGES

1. The legacy `qb export --format=html-v1` option has been removed. Use `--format=html` instead.
2. Plugin API: `onNoteSave` now receives an object rather than a note ID. Plugins that haven't been updated will log a warning and skip the hook. See the migration guide in the docs.

FIXES

- Fixed a crash when pasting tables with merged cells (#2210)
- Fixed attachments not being included in workspace backups on Windows (#2187)
- Fixed tag autocomplete suggesting archived tags (#2193)
- Fixed a rare duplicate-note bug when two devices edited offline (#2145)

UPGRADING

Run `qb update` or download from the releases page. Back up your workspace first; 4.2.0 includes a one-way index migration the first time it opens a workspace.

Thanks to the 14 community contributors who helped with this release.

The Quillbase team

You get these notes because you subscribed to release announcements. Manage preferences in your account settings."}

{"subject": "Hive notes: winter prep for Greywater Beekeepers", "body": "Hello all,

- Heft your hives. If they feel light, you can fit fondant on top of the crown board.

DON'T

{"subject": "Bench Notes #47", "body": "Hi,

Short one this week.

I finished the walnut side table. The drawer finally runs smoothly after I stopped overthinking the runners and just waxed them. Lesson: wax early.

Three things I read or watched:

Elliot

{"subject": "Night Sky Notes: Leonids, a quiet moon, and a planet to find", "body": "Dear stargazers,

THE LEONIDS
Peak is expected the night of 17 to 18 November. With the Moon in a thin crescent, skies should be pleasantly dark. Expect around 10 to 15 meteors per hour after midnight. Face east, give your eyes 20 minutes to adjust, and bring a blanket.

PLANET SPOTTING
Saturn sits high in the southern sky after dusk, a steady, yellowish point. Through even a small telescope its rings are visible.

CLUB NIGHT
The Dunmore Astronomical Society meets Friday 13 November at the community observatory, 7:30 p.m. Weather permitting, we'll have three telescopes set up.

TIP OF THE MONTH
Use a red torch to preserve night vision. Cover a regular torch with red cellophane and a rubber band.

Clear skies,
Henrik"}

{"subject": "The Fathom Report: deep-sea notes for curious people (Issue 63)", "body": "Welcome back, fathomers.

This issue: a fish with a transparent head, a squabble over seabed mining language, and why we still know more about the surface of Mars than the ocean floor.

THE CREATURE
Researchers from the Aldermoor Oceanographic Institute have released new footage of a barreleye filmed at 800 metres. Its eyes swivel beneath a clear, fluid-filled dome. Yes, really. The clip is 40 seconds long and strangely calming.

THE POLICY
Delegates are still arguing over whether 'precautionary approach' should be binding or advisory in the draft seabed minerals text. Our plain-English explainer is below. No jargon, no sighing.

THE NUMBER
26%. That's the share of the global seafloor mapped to modern high resolution. It was 19% five years ago.

READER MAIL
Solveig from Tromsø asked whether the glowing plankton she saw from a ferry was bioluminescence or sea sparkle. Answer: probably dinoflagellates. Lovely either way.

Until next fortnight, stay curious and keep a little salt on your tongue.

Orla Venning
Editor, The Fathom Report"}

{"subject": "Chapter & Verse: five books for a long November", "body": "Hello reader,

It's the season of early dark and second cups of tea. Here's what I've been reading, and what I think you might enjoy.

1. THE LIGHTHOUSE ARITHMETIC by Hanne Vogler
A quiet, precise novel about two sisters inheriting a decommissioned lighthouse. Slow, but rewarding.

2. SALT LEDGER by Dev Raghunathan
Short stories set in a failing port town. Brutal and funny, sometimes in the same sentence.

3. A FIELD GUIDE TO LOSING THINGS by Marguerite Osei
Essays on memory and misplaced objects. Keep a pencil nearby.

4. THE LAST CARTOGRAPHER by Ansel Tripp
Fantasy with an unusually thoughtful magic system based on maps. Book one of three.

5. NIGHT TRAINS TO NOWHERE by Cass Delacroix-Ng
A crime caper on the sleeper routes of a fictional Europe. Pure fun.

FROM THE SHOP
Our independent bookshop's winter reading bundles are back: three paperbacks, wrapped, with a handwritten note, £24.

Happy reading,
Petra
Chapter & Verse Books, 8 Millwright Lane"}

{"subject": "The Larder Ledger: quince season, a new dumpling counter, and where to get the good rye", "body": "Hello again, neighbours,

Slice thin, simmer slowly with a split vanilla pod and a strip of lemon peel, and in about two hours they turn the colour of a rusty sunset.

THIS WEEK'S FINDS

1. Pocket & Pleat opened on Fenwick Street. It's a six-stool dumpling counter run by two cousins, Ines and Dario Valcourt. The pork and chive is solid, but the real star is the brown-butter mushroom dumpling with pickled walnut. Cash only until the card reader arrives, which they say is "any day now" (they have been saying that since Tuesday).

2. The good rye. Hollin Bakehouse is now selling a 70% rye on Thursdays only. It sells out by 10am. I got there at 10:20 and wept quietly into a cardigan.

3. Closing: Mrs. Pellam's Tea Room is shutting at the end of the month after 31 years. Go for the lemon drizzle and say thank you.

RECIPE OF THE WEEK: Quince and Cheddar Toasties
Butter two slices of sourdough. Layer sharp cheddar and a few slices of poached quince. Fry slowly until the cheese gives up. Eat standing at the counter.

Reply and tell me what you're cooking. Best reader recipe gets a jar of my plum chutney.

Hungrily yours,
Margo

{"subject": "Sky Notes for November – Leonids, a tidy Jupiter, and clear-night forecast", "body": "Eastfield Astronomical Society
Monthly Sky Notes, November

HIGHLIGHTS

Leonid meteor shower: peaks overnight on 17–18 November. This year the Moon is a thin waning crescent, so skies should be decently dark. Expect 10–15 meteors an hour from a dark site after midnight. Face east-ish and give your eyes twenty minutes to adjust.

Jupiter: well placed in the evening, rising in the east by around 8pm and high up before dawn. Even a small telescope shows the four Galilean moons and the dark equatorial bands. Great for beginners.

Saturn: still visible low in the south-west after dusk, though the rings are narrowing as they tilt toward edge-on. A subtle but fascinating change.

SOCIETY NEWS
- Observing night: Saturday 15 November at Pike Hill field, from 7pm, weather permitting. We will confirm by 4pm on the day via the members' list. Bring a flask, a red torch, and an extra layer. Then another extra layer.
- Beginners' workshop: 'Collimating your Newtonian,' Wednesday 26 November, 7:30pm at the library annexe. Bring your scope if you have one.
- The club's 8-inch Dobsonian is available to borrow for members. See Alfonso to sign it out. Please return it with the caps on.

A note on light pollution: the new car park floodlights at the retail park are still too bright. Our letter to the council has gone out and we'll let you know the reply.

Clear skies,
Noor Ibekwe
Observations Secretary, Eastfield Astronomical Society"}

{"subject": "Plumbline 4.2 released: faster diffs, new export options, and two breaking changes", "body": "Plumbline 4.2.0 - Release Notes
Released November 4, 2026

Highlights
- Diff engine rewritten. Large-file comparisons are roughly 3x faster in our benchmarks (your results will vary, particularly with files containing very long lines).
- New export formats: Markdown and CSV are now available from the Share menu.
- Workspace search now supports quoted phrases and the NOT operator.

Improvements
- Keyboard shortcut cheat sheet added (press ? anywhere).
- Dark mode contrast improved in the comment sidebar.
- Reduced memory use when more than 20 tabs are open.

Bug fixes
- Fixed a crash when pasting an image into a comment thread on a resolved item.
- Fixed timestamps showing the wrong timezone for users in half-hour offset regions.
- Corrected an issue where archived projects still appeared in autocomplete.

Breaking changes
1. The legacy /v1/snapshots endpoint has been removed. Use /v2/snapshots. Migration guide: docs.plumbline.example/migrate-v2
2. The config option "autoMerge" now defaults to false. If you relied on the old default, add "autoMerge": true to your plumbline.json.

Known issues
- Export to CSV may drop trailing empty columns. A fix is planned for 4.2.1.

Upgrade with your package manager or download from the usual place. Questions? Reply to this email or visit the community forum.

The Plumbline team
Brightfen Labs"}

{"subject": "Skywatch Bulletin: Leonids, a cold-weather observing guide, and the club's loaner telescope", "body": "NORTHFIELD AMATEUR ASTRONOMY CLUB
November Skywatch Bulletin

THE LEONIDS
The Leonid meteor shower peaks around the night of Nov 17-18. This isn't one of the great storm years, so expect a modest rate, maybe 10 to 15 meteors an hour under dark skies. Best viewing is after midnight, when the constellation Leo climbs high in the east. You don't need a telescope. A reclining chair, a warm blanket and about an hour of patience will do.

CLUB OBSERVING NIGHT
Saturday, Nov 15, from dusk at Cobb's Hill field (follow the gravel lane past the red barn). Targets include the Andromeda Galaxy, the Double Cluster and, if it's clear, Saturn's rings. Please use red flashlights only.

COLD-WEATHER TIPS
1. Layers, then more layers. Your feet will get cold first.
2. Keep a thermos handy. Hot chocolate counts as equipment.
3. Let your telescope sit outside for 30 minutes before observing so the mirror can adjust to the temperature. This will sharpen the view.
4. Never wipe frost off optics with a cloth. Let it clear naturally.

LOANER TELESCOPE PROGRAM
The club's 8-inch Dobsonian is available for members to borrow for two weeks at a time. Currently reserved through Nov 29. Sign up with Gerald Pruitt (gerald@northfieldastro.example).

MEMBER PHOTO OF THE MONTH
Congratulations to Leilani Ostrowski for her image of the Pleiades, captured from her back porch with a borrowed camera and what she described as "stubbornness."

Clear skies,
The NAAC Committee"}

Welcome to the last Maple & Thread newsletter of the year! Pour something warm. This one is a bit long.

QUILT-ALONG FINALE
The Autumn Leaves quilt-along officially ends Nov 30. If you're stuck on the border (many of you are, judging by your emails), here's the secret: cut your border strips a little longer than the pattern says, then trim to fit. Every single time. We've also posted a short video on mitering corners.

Submit your finished quilt photos at maplethread.example/gallery by Dec 5 to be entered in the drawing for a fat-quarter bundle.

A GUIDE TO THRIFTING FABRIC
I spent a Saturday morning at three secondhand shops and came away with 11 yards of cotton for under $20. My tips:
- Check for fading along fold lines.
- Smell test. If it smells like a basement, a vinegar soak helps, but no guarantees.
- Look for tablecloths and bedsheets. Percale sheets are wonderful for quilt backing.
- Always prewash before cutting. Always.

READER MAIL
Beatrix from Tulloch wrote asking whether it's "cheating" to use a longarm service. My answer: absolutely not. The goal is a finished quilt that makes someone warm.

NEXT TIME
In the new year we begin a beginner-friendly Log Cabin project with a pattern designed for scraps. Start saving yours.

Happy stitching,
Corinna Hatch
Maple & Thread"}

{"subject": "Seedling Notes: what to plant, what to cover, what to ignore (Zone 7)", "body": "Hello gardeners,

First frost arrived Monday night, so here's the short list.

DO NOW
- Plant garlic cloves, pointy end up, about 2 inches deep. Mulch with straw.
- Cover tender greens with row fabric overnight.
- Lift dahlia tubers and store them somewhere cool and dry.

CAN WAIT
- Pruning roses. Wait until late winter.
- Dividing perennials. Spring is fine.

IGNORE
- Advice that says you must rake every leaf. Leave some under shrubs. The beetles and toads will thank you.

READER PHOTO OF THE WEEK
Carla in Dunmore sent a picture of a pumpkin shaped exactly like a sleeping cat. We are still smiling.

Seed swap is Saturday the 22nd at the community hall, 10-1. Bring envelopes and a pen.

Happy digging,
Otis
Seedling Notes"}

{"subject": "Bird notes from the Wexcombe Estuary — what's new on the mudflats", "body": "Hello birders,

Autumn passage is winding down, but the estuary is far from quiet.

HIGHLIGHTS THIS FORTNIGHT
- Around 3,200 wigeon counted on the high tide roost, our best October–November total in six years.
- A juvenile spoonbill lingered near the sluice for four days (last seen Nov 1).
- Two short-eared owls hunting over the saltmarsh at dusk. Best viewed from the east hide at about 4pm.
- Water pipits are back on the creek edge.

VISITOR NOTES
The west boardwalk is closed for repairs until at least the 20th. Please use the east path and stick to marked routes; the roost is sensitive to disturbance.

UPCOMING WALKS
Sat Nov 14, 9am: Beginners' winter wader walk (bring a flask)
Sun Nov 29, 8am: Full tide count, volunteers needed

Please log your sightings on the group's shared sheet. Even common species help.

Happy birding,
Gideon Pryce
Wexcombe Estuary Birdwatching Group"}

{"subject": "Recipe you asked for (finally)", "body": "Hi Auntie Joyce,

Here's the plum cake recipe, as promised. Fair warning: Grandma never wrote down amounts, so I've guessed from memory and from three failed attempts.

- 250g plums, halved
- 180g flour
- 120g sugar (a bit less if the plums are sweet)
- 2 eggs
- 100g butter, softened
- 1 tsp baking powder
- cinnamon, as much as feels right

Bake at 180°C for about 45 minutes, until a knife comes out clean. Plums go face up. If it comes out soggy, you did it right, because that's how hers was.

Tell me how it goes!
Pia"}

{"subject": "Invitation: Housewarming, Nov 21", "body": "Hi all,

After eleven months of boxes, we finally have a sofa. Come to our housewarming on Saturday, November 21st, from 4pm onward, at 38 Alder Row (the green door, buzzer says Okafor-Lindqvist).

We'll have chili, a vegetarian version, and far too much cake. Bring nothing but yourselves. Please RSVP by the 14th so we know how many chairs to borrow from the neighbours.

Ben & Adaeze"}

{"subject": "Sorry I missed your call", "body": "Hi Dad,

Sorry I missed your call earlier, I was in back-to-back meetings and my phone was in my bag. Nothing urgent, I hope. I'm free tomorrow evening after 7 if you want to ring then. Also, did the parcel arrive? The tracking said Tuesday.

Talk soon,
Halvor"}

{"subject": "Borrowing your ladder", "body": "Hey Gus,

Is your extension ladder still in the garage? The gutters are overflowing and I'd rather not wait for the landlord. I can pick it up Sunday morning and have it back by lunch. I'll bring coffee as a bribe.

Cheers,
Nadia"}

{"subject": "Photos from the reunion", "body": "Hi everyone,

As promised, the shared album from the Wexcombe family reunion is here: the link is in the message below. There are about 140 photos, and I've tagged the ones where Great-Aunt Philippa is mid-story, which is most of them. Add your own if you have any, the album is open until the end of the month.

Thanks to all who came. Same time next year?

Aunt Dorothea

[album link omitted]"}

{"subject": "New job, new city", "body": "Dear Tomasz,

I know I've been terrible at keeping in touch, so here's the big news in one go: I accepted the position in Gdansk and I move on the first of December. It's a smaller flat than I'm used to but it has a balcony facing the harbour.

I'd love to see you before I go. Are you free for dinner any evening the week of the 23rd? My treat, since I'm abandoning you.

Your friend,
Elzbieta"}

{"subject": "Saturday still on?", "body": "Hey Marit,

Just checking we're still good for Saturday. I can pick you up around 9:30 if you're okay with the drive out to Halvorsen Lake. I'll bring the thermos and extra gloves since you always forget yours.

Let me know if the forecast changes your mind.

Tobias"}

{"subject": "So sorry about Grandpa Leif", "body": "Dear Annika,

I heard the news from your mother this morning and I wanted to write right away. I'm so very sorry. Your grandfather was one of the kindest people I ever met. I still remember him teaching us to play cribbage on that screened porch, cheating shamelessly and laughing the whole time.

Please don't feel you need to reply. I'm thinking of you and your family. If it would help, I can bring over dinner this week or just come sit with you. Say the word.

With love,
Dorothea"}

{"subject": "Can I borrow your tile saw?", "body": "Hi Ravi,

Small favour. I'm finally redoing the bathroom floor and the rental place wants $60 a day for a wet saw. You still have the one from your patio project? I'd need it for a weekend, maybe Saturday through Monday morning. Happy to return it cleaned, with a new blade if the old one's worn, plus beer.

Thanks!
Cal"}

{"subject": "We're engaged!!", "body": "Everyone,

Devon asked me on Tuesday at the end of the pier in Pelham Cove, in the rain, with a ring he'd hidden inside a bag of kettle corn. I said yes before he finished the question.

No date yet, we're just enjoying it. Wanted you to hear it from us first. Call me this weekend, I want to hear all your screaming.

Love,
Priya"}

{"subject": "Fwd: recipe you asked about", "body": "Mom,

Here's Aunt Bettina's plum cake recipe, typed up from the photo. The oven temp in her handwriting looks like 175 but I think she meant 375. Her cakes were never pale, so go with 375.

- 1 1/2 cups flour
- 1 cup sugar
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 cup butter
- 2 eggs
- plums, halved

No need to write back. Just enjoy.

Jonas"}

{"subject": "Housewarming, Nov 21 (finally!)", "body": "Hi all,

We've been in the new place for four months and it's still half boxes, but we're having people over on Saturday, November 21, from 4 pm onward. Chili, cornbread, and a lot of folding chairs. Kids welcome, dogs also welcome (ours is friendly, mostly).

Please RSVP by the 14th so I know how much chili to make. Address is 88 Wren Street, the green door.

Hugs,
Lucia & Hamid"}
{"subject": "re: your message", "body": "Sorry I missed your call. Work's been a mess. Can we talk Sunday evening? I have some news too.\n\nE."}

{"subject": "Photos from the reunion", "body": "Hi cousins,

I finally sorted through everything from the August reunion. The shared album is here: the link is in the message below this one. There are about 140 photos, and yes, I included the one of Uncle Gus asleep in the hammock. You're welcome.

If you'd like any printed, let me know by the end of the month and I'll place one order for all of us.

Best,
Wilhelmina"}

{"subject": "Need a place to crash in March?", "body": "Hey Sam,

I'm coming to your city for a conference March 9-12 and my hotel budget got cut. Any chance I could take your couch for three nights? I promise to be out early, cook at least one dinner, and not touch your plants. If it's a bad time, totally fine, I'll find something.

Let me know when you can!
Noor"}

{"subject": "Thank you for the soup", "body": "Dear Mrs. Okafor,

The soup you left on our porch was the best thing that happened to us all week. Baby Theo has been up every two hours and we were running on crackers. We returned your container, washed, in the mailbox.

Thank you for thinking of us. No reply needed, just wanted you to know it mattered.

Warmly,
Grace and Felix"}

{"subject": "Re: Saturday - can you pick up Dad?", "body": "Hi Marit,

Yes, I can do it. I'll be at his place by 10:15 so we have time before the service starts at 11. Does he still need the cane in the car or has he gone back to the walker? Just want to make sure I fold things right.

I'll bring the umbrella too, forecast looks grim.

See you there,
Olav"}

{"subject": "Thinking of you", "body": "Dear Hannah,

I just heard about your grandmother from Bea this morning and I'm so sorry. I remember her sending you those ridiculous knitted sweaters at university and how proud you were wearing them.

You don't need to reply to this. I just wanted you to know I'm thinking of you. If you'd like company, or someone to drop off a casserole and leave without making you talk, say the word.

With love,
Priya"}

{"subject": "We're moving!!", "body": "Hey everyone,

Big news from the Delacroix-Nwosu household: we got the keys to the house on Alder Lane! We move on the 22nd of this month. The kids are already fighting over who gets the room with the window seat.

No need to do anything, just wanted you to hear it from us first. Housewarming to come once we've unpacked (so, probably spring).

Love,
Tobias, Ada, Kemi and Jonah"}

{"subject": "Can I borrow your tile saw?", "body": "Hey Declan,

Quick favour. I'm finally redoing the bathroom floor and I remember you had a wet tile saw in your garage. Any chance I could borrow it for a weekend? I'd pick it up Friday evening and return it Sunday night, cleaned, with a six-pack as a thank-you.

Let me know if that works or if you're using it.

Cheers,
Greg"}

{"subject": "Dinner on the 14th?", "body": "Dear Auntie Lucinda,

Marcus and I would love to have you over for dinner on Saturday the 14th around 6:30. I'm making the lamb dish you taught me, though I make no promises about the crust.

Could you let me know by Wednesday if you can make it, and whether there's anything you can't eat these days? Uncle Rafe is of course welcome too if he's feeling up to it.

Love,
Sophie"}

{"subject": "Sorry I missed your call", "body": "Hi Mum,

Sorry I missed your call last night, I was stuck at work late and then fell asleep on the sofa in my coat. Everything's fine, nothing to worry about! I'll ring you Sunday after lunch when I'm properly awake.

Yes, I'm still coming for Christmas. I booked the train for the 23rd, getting in around four. Could you ask Dad whether he can meet me at the station, or I'll get a taxi?

Love you,
Nina"}

{"subject": "Wedding invitation - Kasimir & Elodie", "body": "Dear Anselm,

Elodie and I are getting married on Saturday, 6 June, at the Hollis Mill barn outside Kettering, and it would mean the world to have you there. Ceremony at 2pm, dinner and dancing to follow. There's a block of rooms held at the Crown Inn under our name until the end of February.

A formal invitation is on its way by post, but I wanted you to have the date early. Please RSVP by replying here or calling me whenever.

Your old flatmate,
Kaz"}

{"subject": "Did you hear about Mr. Okafor?", "body": "Hi Ruth,

I wasn't sure whether you'd heard. Mr. Okafor from our old street passed away last Tuesday. The funeral is next Friday at St. Brendan's at noon, with tea afterwards in the church hall. I'm planning to go and thought you might want to come along, since he was so kind to us as kids. I can drive if you'd like to share a ride.

Let me know either way, and I'll save you a seat.

Yours,
Daniel"}

{"subject": "Re: Saturday ferry?", "body": "Hi Odalys,

Yes, the 9:40 works for me. I'll bring the thermos and those awful ginger biscuits you like. Can you grab the tickets? I'll pay you back in cash when we meet at the dock.

If the wind picks up like they're saying, we may need a Plan B. Let me know what you think by Friday night.

Tomasz"}

{"subject": "Grandpa Ruben", "body": "Dear Marguerite,

I heard this morning about your grandfather. I'm so sorry. I remember him teaching us to play dominoes on your porch, cheating shamelessly and laughing the whole time. He made every summer feel bigger.

You don't need to reply to this. I just wanted you to know I'm thinking of you and your family. If it would help, I can drop off dinner on Thursday, no need to talk, I'll leave it on the step.

With love,
Brenna"}

{"subject": "We're moving! (finally)", "body": "Hey everyone,

Big news from the Okonkwo-Hale household: we got the keys to the house on Larkspur Lane! We're moving on December 12th. It's smaller than we hoped but it has a fig tree and a very strange pink bathroom that I'm weirdly attached to.

New address is below. No need to respond, just update your holiday card lists. Hugs to all.

14 Larkspur Lane, Wendover Falls

Priya"}

{"subject": "Can you take Biscuit for a weekend?", "body": "Hi Dad,

I know it's a lot to ask, but Dani and I have been invited to her cousin's wedding in Portland, Nov 21-23, and the kennel is fully booked. Could Biscuit stay with you? He's mostly calm now, though he still barks at the mail carrier.

I'll bring his food, bed, and the ridiculous squeaky carrot. Please let me know by Sunday so I can try other options if it's not good for you.

Thanks,
Leo"}

{"subject": "photos from the lake", "body": "Aunt Cecilia,

Attached (well, linked, the files were huge) are the photos from the lake weekend: https://photos.example.invalid/lake-trip-2026. The one of you holding the tiny fish is my favorite.

Mom says hello and that she's still sore from the canoe.

Love,
Juniper"}

{"subject": "Rain check on dinner?", "body": "Hey Wes,

So sorry to do this, but Ingrid has a fever and I think I should stay home tonight. Can we move our dinner to next week? Tuesday or Thursday would both work. I owe you a really good bottle of wine for the short notice.

Hope you haven't already booked the table. Let me know.

Sam"}

{"subject": "Your 40th!!", "body": "Hello dear friend of Rosalind,

Rosalind turns 40 on January 17th and her husband Gabe is planning a surprise party at Pelham's Boathouse, 7pm. Please keep it secret! Dress is festive casual. If you can come, RSVP to me directly (not to Rosalind, obviously) by December 20th.

If you have a funny story or photo of her, send it along and we'll put them in a slideshow.

Thanks!
Gabe's sister, Noor"}

{"subject": "Re: recipe", "body": "Nana,

I made your lamb stew last night and it came out almost right. Almost. Something was missing. Was it the allspice or did you put a little vinegar in at the end? Dev said it needed more salt but he says that about everything.

Call me when you have a minute, or just write back. No rush.

Xo, Anika"}

{"subject": "thank you", "body": "Dear Hollis and Pam,

Thank you so much for letting us stay with you through the whole furnace mess. Three nights turned into six and you never once made us feel like a burden. The kids are still talking about the pancake breakfast.

The heat is fixed now and we're home. We'd love to have you over soon so we can return the favour.

Warmly,
Carla and Nico"}

{"subject": "Car trouble, sorry", "body": "Mick, I'm stuck outside Harlow with a flat and a spare that's also flat, which feels like an accomplishment. Could you possibly pick me up? I'm by the gas station with the giant plastic cow. Phone's at 8% so email is easier than calling, but if you see this, please call the tow place first, number's on the back of the card in my glovebox... actually I'm not near it. Just come get me. Thanks, brother.\n\nRay"}
